props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who buys the shearing of his fellow's flock -- [if the seller kept some, the seller is obligated]; who is the tanna for whom, where there is residue with the seller, we go after the seller?
[the mishna's other clause:] the seller did not keep any -- the buyer is obligated
Rav Chisda: it is R' Yehuda
one who sells tree stalks within his field -- he gives pe'ah for each and every one
R' Yehuda: when? when the field-owner did not keep [any]
but if the field-owner kept, he gives pe'ah for all
Rav Chisda's own statement, cited by Rava: and that is when the field-owner began to harvest
and if you say: here too, [the seller is obligated] when he began to shear
granted there: 'and when you reap the harvest of your land' (Lev 19:9) is written -- from when he began to reap he is obligated in the whole field
but here, from when he began to shear he is not obligated in his whole flock
rather, Rava: it is this tanna [of the innards mishna]
he said to him 'sell me the innards of this cow' and the gifts were in them -- he gives them to the priest and does not deduct from the price
he bought from him by weight -- he gives them to the priest and deducts from the price
evidently, a person does not sell the priest's gifts
here too, a person does not sell the priest's gifts [the first shearing]
the seller kept -- the seller is obligated, for the buyer says to him: the priest's gift is with you
he did not keep -- the buyer is obligated, for the seller says to him: the priest's gift I did not sell you
